questions.stem: Kedu isiokwu kwesịrị edemede arụmụka?
options: Obodo mepere emepe dị mma karịa ime obodo
Otu e si esi ofe egwusi
questions.explanation: A claim that one place is better than another can be argued for or against: argumentative essay (arụmụka).

questions.stem: Edemede na-akọ ihe mere n'usoro ka o si mee bụ edemede
questions.explanation: An essay that recounts events in order is narrative (edemede akụkọ).

questions.stem: Mkpụrụedemede Igbo dị ole?
questions.explanation: Standard Igbo has 36 letters: 8 vowels and 28 consonants (including digraphs such as ch, gb, kp, nw).

questions.stem: Ụdaume ole dị n'asụsụ Igbo?
questions.explanation: The eight Igbo vowels are a, e, i, ị, o, ọ, u, ụ.

questions.stem: Mgbochiume ole dị na mkpụrụedemede Igbo?
questions.explanation: 36 letters minus 8 vowels gives 28 consonants.

questions.stem: Na ndakọrịta ụdaume, ụdaume ndị na-eso "a" n'otu otu bụ
questions.explanation: Igbo vowel harmony groups: (a, ị, ọ, ụ) and (e, i, o, u).

questions.stem: Mkpụrụokwu ole dị n'okwu "akwụkwọ"?
questions.explanation: kw is a single consonant, so the word divides a-kwụ-kwọ.

questions.stem: N'okwu ole n'ime ndị a ka mgbochiume "n" bụ mkpụrụokwu n'onwe ya?
questions.explanation: In nna the first n is a syllabic nasal: n-na.

questions.stem: Akara a na-eji egosi ụda ala bụ
questions.explanation: Low tone is marked with the grave accent; high with the acute; downstep with the macron.

questions.stem: Kedu nke bụ aha n'ime ndị a?
questions.explanation: Oche (chair) is a noun; ịga is a verb, mana a conjunction, ha a pronoun.

questions.stem: Kedu nke bụ nnọchiaha n'ime ndị a?
questions.explanation: Ha (they) replaces a noun: a pronoun (nnọchiaha).

questions.stem: N'ahịrịokwu "Ada riri ji", onye mere ihe ahụ bụ
questions.explanation: Ada performs the action of eating: the subject.

questions.stem: "Iri abụọ na ise" bụ
questions.explanation: Iri abụọ = 20; na ise = and five: 25.

questions.stem: "Narị abụọ" bụ
questions.explanation: Narị = hundred; narị abụọ = 200.

questions.stem: "Anyị" bụ nnọchiaha nke
questions.explanation: Anyị (we) is first person plural.

questions.stem: Kedu okwu agbaziri agbazi n'ime ndị a?
questions.explanation: Tebụl is borrowed from English "table"; the others are native Igbo words.

questions.stem: Kedu nke bụ njikọ n'ime ndị a?
questions.explanation: Mana (but) joins clauses: a conjunction.

questions.stem: Akụkọ ifo bụ akụkọ
options: e kere eke nke a na-akọrọ ụmụaka ka ha mụta ihe
eziokwu banyere ndị dike gara aga
nke na-enweghị ihe ọ bụla ọ na-akụzi
questions.explanation: Folktales (ifo) are imaginative stories told to children to teach morals.

questions.stem: Akụkọ na-akọ otu ụwa ma ọ bụ ihe si malite bụ
questions.explanation: Myths (akụkọ okike/mmalite) explain origins.

questions.stem: Akụkọ banyere ndị dike nke oge gara aga bụ
questions.explanation: Legends (akụkọ dike) tell of heroes of the past.

questions.stem: Ajụjụ a na-ajụ ka e chee echiche tupu a zaa ya, dịka egwuregwu, bụ
questions.explanation: Riddles (agwụgwa) are question-and-answer puzzles.

questions.stem: Onye dere akwụkwọ akụkọ "Omenuko"?
questions.explanation: Pita Nwana's Omenuko (1933) is regarded as the first Igbo novel.

questions.stem: Akwụkwọ e dere ka e mee ya n'ihu ọha bụ
questions.explanation: A play written for performance is drama (ejije).

questions.stem: Akwụkwọ nwere amaokwu na ahịrị dị iche iche bụ akwụkwọ
questions.explanation: Poetry (abụ) is arranged in stanzas (amaokwu) and lines.

questions.stem: Ụbọchị ahịa anọ dị n'izu Igbo bụ
questions.explanation: The Igbo market week (izu) has four days: Eke, Orie, Afọ and Nkwọ.

questions.stem: "Nnọọ" bụ ekele a na-ekele
questions.explanation: Nnọọ means welcome.

questions.stem: Ihe mbụ onye Igbo na-enye ọbịa bịara n'ụlọ ya bụ
questions.explanation: Kola nut (ọjị) is presented first to welcome a visitor.

questions.stem: Ọmụgwọ bụ mgbe
options: nne nwaanyị mụrụ nwa na-abịa ilekọta ya na nwa ọhụrụ
questions.explanation: Omugwo is postnatal care, usually by the new mother's own mother.

questions.stem: Ememe e ji eri ji ọhụrụ bụ
questions.explanation: The New Yam festival is iri ji (iwa ji); akwamozu is a funeral.

questions.stem: Nwa a na-ekwere na ọ na-anwụ ma na-alọghachi ọzọ bụ
questions.explanation: Ọgbanje is believed to die and return repeatedly.

questions.stem: Ụmụ nwaanyị a mụrụ n'otu ụmụnna ma lụọ di n'ebe ọzọ bụ
questions.explanation: Ụmụada are the married daughters of a lineage, an influential group.

questions.stem: Nze na Ọzọ bụ otu
questions.explanation: Nze na Ọzọ is a prestigious title society.

questions.stem: Ọfọ bụ akara
questions.explanation: Ọfọ is a symbol of authority and truth/justice.

questions.stem: Mmọnwụ, Ekpe na Odo bụ ụdị
questions.explanation: They are societies (abamaba), as listed under institutions.

questions.stem: Ọrụ "ịgba nta" bụ
questions.explanation: Ịgba nta is hunting.

questions.stem:
Dee edemede (ihe dị ka okwu narị atọ) n'otu n'ime isiokwu ndị a:
(a) Ahịa obodo anyị.
(b) Obodo mepere emepe dị mma karịa ime obodo.
(c) Akwụkwọ ozi i degaara enyi gị banyere ezumike gị. [25 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
10 marks: Content: relevant, well-developed ideas suited to the essay type chosen
5 marks: Organisation: introduction, logical paragraphs, conclusion; correct letter format for (c)
7 marks: Expression: idiomatic Standard Igbo with appropriate proverbs and varied sentences
3 marks: Mechanical accuracy: standard orthography, spelling and punctuation
questions.explanation: A strong essay picks one topic, plans an introduction, focused paragraphs and a conclusion, writes idiomatic Standard Igbo with apt proverbs, and follows the standard orthography.

questions.stem:
(a) Dee ụdaume Igbo asatọ. [4 marks]
(b) Kọwaa ndakọrịta ụdaume, kesaa ụdaume ndị ahụ n'otu abụọ ha. [6 marks]
(c) Kee okwu ndị a n'mkpụrụokwu: akwụkwọ, nna, ọkụkọ. [5 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
4 marks: a, e, i, ị, o, ọ, u, ụ (all eight)
2 marks: Vowel harmony: vowels in a simple word come from the same group
4 marks: Group 1: a, ị, ọ, ụ; Group 2: e, i, o, u (2 each)
2 marks: a-kwụ-kwọ
1 mark: n-na
2 marks: ọ-kụ-kọ
questions.explanation: The eight vowels split into harmony groups (a, ị, ọ, ụ) and (e, i, o, u). akwụkwọ = a-kwụ-kwọ; nna = n-na; ọkụkọ = ọ-kụ-kọ.

questions.stem: Kọwaa ụdị okwu ise n'asụsụ Igbo, nye ihe atụ abụọ maka nke ọ bụla. [15 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
3 marks: Aha (noun): names person, place, thing; e.g. oche, Ada, ụlọ
3 marks: Ngwaa (verb): shows action; e.g. ịga, iri, ịgba
3 marks: Nnọchiaha (pronoun): replaces a noun; e.g. ha, anyị, ọ
3 marks: Nkọwaaha (adjective): describes a noun; e.g. ọma, ọcha
3 marks: Njikọ (conjunction): joins words/clauses; e.g. na, mana (accept other classes correctly explained)
questions.explanation: Noun (oche), verb (ịga), pronoun (ha, anyị), adjective (ọma, ọcha) and conjunction (na, mana), each defined with two examples.

questions.stem:
(a) Gịnị bụ akụkọ ifo? [3 marks]
(b) Dee njirimara akụkọ ifo anọ. [8 marks]
(c) Dee uru abụọ akụkọ ifo bara. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
3 marks: Folktale: an imaginative oral story, often about animals or people, told mainly in the evening to entertain and teach
8 marks: Any four (2 each): opening and closing formulas; songs within the story with audience participation; animal characters such as mbe (tortoise); a moral lesson at the end; told by elders in the evening; repetition
4 marks: Any two (2 each): teaches morals; entertains; preserves culture and language; develops listening and imagination
questions.explanation: Ifo are imaginative tales told in the evening, with songs, animal characters such as the tortoise and a moral ending; they teach, entertain and preserve culture.

questions.stem:
(a) Kọwaa ọdịiche dị n'etiti akwụkwọ akụkọ (prose), abụ na ejije. [9 marks]
(b) Kọwaa ihe atọ onye na-agụ akwụkwọ ejije kwesịrị ilebara anya. [6 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
3 marks: Prose (akwụkwọ akụkọ): continuous narrative in paragraphs and chapters, told by a narrator
3 marks: Poetry (abụ): arranged in lines and stanzas (amaokwu), with rhythm and imagery
3 marks: Drama (ejije): written in dialogue for performance, divided into acts and scenes, with stage directions
6 marks: Any three (2 each): characters; plot; theme; setting; language/style; conflict
questions.explanation: Prose narrates in paragraphs; poetry uses lines and stanzas; drama uses dialogue for performance. A reader of drama examines characters, plot, theme, setting and language.

questions.stem:
Kọwaa ememe iri ji n'obodo Igbo:
(a) oge a na-eme ya; [3 marks]
(b) otu e si eme ya; [8 marks]
(c) uru ọ bara. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
3 marks: Time: at harvest of the new yam, around August to October, after the planting season
8 marks: Description (award up to 8): no new yam eaten before the festival; the eldest/traditional ruler offers yam and thanks to Ala/ancestors; the first new yam is roasted and eaten; feasting, dancing, masquerades and visits; family members return home
4 marks: Any two (2 each): thanksgiving for harvest; unity and reunion; preserving culture; marks start of eating new yam
questions.explanation: Iri ji is held at the new yam harvest. After rites of thanks by elders, the new yam is roasted and eaten, followed by feasting and masquerades. It gives thanks, unites families and preserves culture.
